chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
Regarding the people of the jizyah (taxpayers), is anything taken from their wealth and their livestock besides the jizyah? He said: No.
ai.seo_question: What taxes can be taken from non-Muslim taxpayers besides jizyah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the jizyah is the sole compulsory fiscal obligation for non-Muslim subjects (ahl al-dhimma), prohibiting the imposition of additional arbitrary taxes on their wealth or livestock. This ruling underscores the principle of fiscal justice in Shia jurisprudence, ensuring that the tribute remains a fixed covenant rather than a source of exploitative revenue. It reflects the broader Islamic legal tradition of protecting the economic stability of minority communities under Muslim rule.
